paragraphs.text: Eric and his parents stood outside their house.
They were watching a parade.
A band marched toward them.
Eric saw lots of different instruments.
And then— boom! Ba-boom! Rat-a-tat-tat! Drums!
Drummers banged big drums and little drums.
"Cool!" thought Eric.
Days went by.
Eric couldn't stop thinking about those drums.
At dinner he tapped on the table.
At school he tapped on his books.
In the kitchen he banged pots together.
"Let's go to the garage," Dad said one day.
"Why?" Eric asked.
Dad smiled. "I have a surprise."
Dad took Eric into the garage.
"A drum set!" cried Eric.
It was Dad's old drum set.
The set had three drums and cymbals.
Dad gave Eric the drumsticks.
He showed Eric how to hold them.
Eric hit the drums fast. Tat! Tat! Tat!
Eric banged the cymbals. Clash!
"I hear music!" someone said.
Eric looked up and saw Mom.
She had her guitar.
Dad held up his harmonica.
Eric grinned. "We've got a family band.
Let's play!"
Rosa counted dimes and quarters.
"We have five dollars," she said.
Jo grinned. "Now can we buy that magic kit?"
"Not yet," said Rosa.
"But we can do a magic trick."
"How?" asked Jo.
"First, we need some lemons," said Rosa.
"Then, we'll turn the lemons into money!"
Later the twins set up a table and a sign.
They had pitchers of lemonade and cups.
A boy rode by on a bike.
"Hey!" Rosa shouted.
"Want some lemonade?
It only costs two dollars!"
"Two dollars for lemonade?" said the boy.
"Are you crazy?"
"Ice-cold lemonade!" Rosa shouted to a woman.
The woman looked at the price.
"No, thanks," she said.
"Hmm...," thought Jo.
"I have an idea!"
Soon lots of people were buying lemonade.
"Good idea, Jo," said Rosa.
"Two dollars was too expensive.
Fifty cents is a better price."
"Look!" said Jo.
"We made twenty dollars!
I know what to buy now."
"The magic kit?" asked Rosa.
"Nope," said Jo.
"More lemons!"
It's Career Day.
My class is learning about different jobs.
Miss Wilson is a chef.
She cooks delicious meals.
She works at a restaurant.
Mr. Smith is a photographer.
He takes pictures of babies.
He works at a studio.
Mr. Lewis is a car designer.
He designs cars.
He works at a car company.
Dr. White is a dentist.
She checks people's teeth.
She works at a dentist's office.
Mrs. Jones is a vet.
She takes care of sick animals.
She works at an animal hospital.
Professor Allen is a scientist.
He studies science.
He works at a university.
Career Day is fun! There are lots of fun jobs.
What do you want to be when you grow up?
It's almost Mother’s Day.
I want to do something special for Mom.
Hmm. What can I do?
She's a great mom.
I must think of something amazing.
I know! I'll make a card!
Dear Mom,
I promise to clean my room.
I promise to put away my dirty socks.
I promise to help you wash dishes.
I promise to be nice to my brother.
(I'll even share my games with him!)
I promise to clean up after the dog.
When you say "Wake up," I will listen.
When you say "Time for bed," I won't complain.
When you make broccoli for dinner, I will eat it.
When you're happy, I will dance with you.
When you're sad, I will give you hugs.
I promise all these things.
Love,
Abby
On Mother's Day I run to Mom.
"Here, Mom!" I say.
"Happy Mother's Day!"
My family has a new baby.
He needs lots of things.
He needs a crib and a swing.
He needs bottles and bibs.
He needs diapers and toys and blankets.
Sometimes my baby brother is not fun!
He sleeps a lot.
He eats a lot.
He cries a lot, and he is loud!
Waa! Waa! Waa!
But sometimes my baby brother is lots of fun!
I hold him and rock him.
I read books to him.
I help him play with toys.
And then, best of all . . .
He smiles at me.
I am his big sister!
Allan didn't like high places.
Allan didn't climb ladders.
"No way!"
Allan didn't go on the slide.
"Too scary!"
Allan never jumped off the diving board.
"Not me!"
Allan never climbed tall trees.
"Wait a minute. What's that?"
Allan's cat was in a tree.
It was not a tall tree.
But Allan thought it was a very tall tree.
"I can't leave my cat in the tree."
How could Allan get his cat?
Allan called for help. "Somebody help! Help!
Please get my cat!"
No one answered. Nobody helped.
Allan cried. Then Allan's dad came outside.
"Allan, why are you crying?" he said.
"Dad, my cat is up in the tree.
I can't get it." Allan said.
"Climb up here."
Allan slowly climbed onto his dad's shoulders.
"Are you still scared?" Allan's dad asked.
"No," Allan said.
Allan got the cat and held it.
"Don't worry, kitty. You're safe now."
"Thanks, Dad!" Allan said.
He looked at the tall tree.
"Hmmm. That tree is shorter now!"
This is my little brother, Matt.
This is my big sister, Meg.
He is six years old.
I am ten years old.
She is fourteen years old.
He is younger than me.
She is older than me.
I'm in the middle.
He is one hundred ten centimeters tall.
I am one hundred forty centimeters tall.
She is one hundred sixty centimeters tall.
He is shorter than me.
She is taller than me.
I'm in the middle.
He weighs twenty kilograms.
I weigh forty kilograms.
She weighs fifty kilograms.
He is lighter than me.
She is heavier than me.
I'm in the middle.
Uh-oh. He is mad at her.
She is mad at him.
Oh no! I'm in the middle.
"Look!" Joe pointed to the floor.
"Our Classroom Rules poster!"
Miss Shin picked up the poster.
Dirty footprints covered all the rules.
"Yay!" Teddy shouted. "No more rules!"
Miss Shin frowned.
She put the dirty poster in the trash.
"Time for a class meeting," she said.
Everyone gathered around the teacher.
"What do you think?" she asked.
"Do we need to make rules again?"
"No!" Teddy yelled.
Morgan covered her ears.
Then she raised her hand.
"Yes," said Morgan. "We need rules.
Without rules, the classroom may be too noisy."
Jamal raised his hand next.
"Without rules, kids may forget their manners," he said.
Sadie saw Teddy poking Jamal with a ruler.
She raised her hand.
"Kids may not respect others."
"Hmm," said Miss Shin. "Let's see.
Who thinks we need rules?"
Ten hands went up.
But Teddy's hands stayed down.
"Ugh," Teddy groaned. "I lose."
"Everyone wins, Teddy," said Miss Shin.
"Classroom rules help us learn and have fun.
Let's begin."
Teacher: Good morning, class!
Dan: I didn't bring a pencil. Can I borrow a pencil?
Molly: Sure, here you are.
Dan: I didn't bring an eraser. Can I borrow your eraser?
Molly: Sure, here you go.
Dan: I didn't bring a glue stick. Can I borrow your glue stick?
Molly: Of course, Dan. Here.
Dan: I didn't bring a compass. Can I borrow your compass?
Molly: Okay, Dan. Here you are.
Dan: I didn't bring a ruler. Can I borrow your ruler?
Molly: Fine, Dan. Here.
Dan: I didn't bring a calculator. Can I borrow your calculator?
Molly: Here.
Teacher: It's time to turn in your homework.
Dan: I didn't bring my homework. Can I borrow yours?
Molly: No, Dan! You cannot borrow my homework!
Teacher: Dan, where is your homework?
"Today, you are going to the doctor."
"But I'm not sick, Mom."
"You need a checkup."
"Mom, what is a checkup?"
"The doctor looks at you. He checks that you are healthy."
"Will it be hard?"
"No, it will be easy."
"Oh, I don't know."
"Stick out your tongue, Richard."
"That’s easy. I can stick out my tongue."
"Pull up your shirt."
"That’s too easy. I can pull up my shirt."
"Now, Richard, can you touch your toes?"
"No problem. I can touch my toes."
"Turn your head, Richard. I will look into your ear."
"That’s easy for me. I can turn my head."
"Richard, let's see how much you weigh. Stand on the scales."
"That's really easy. I can stand on the scales."
"How tall are you, Richard? Stand up tall."
"I can stand up tall. Look at me."
"Now I will check your eyes. Please, look into this light."
"Okay. I can look at the light. A checkup is very easy."
"Richard, can you roll up your sleeve?"
"Ha-ha! I can roll up my sleeve. That's easy too."
"Ouch! Ouch!"
"Finished! That was easy for you, Richard."
"I don't know. Ouch."
This is where I sit to watch Mommy cook.
I sit on a stool.
This is where I sit to eat.
I sit on a dining room chair.
This is where my baby brother sits to eat.
He sits in a high chair.
This is where I sit to study.
I sit in a desk chair.
This is where I sit to read.
I sit in an easy chair.
This is where I sit to rock my doll.
I sit in a rocking chair.
This is where my brother sits to ride in the car.
He sits in a car seat.
This is where I sit to fish by the lake.
I sit on a folding chair.
What chairs do you sit on?
New Year's Day is in January.
"Happy New Year!"
Valentine's Day is in February.
"Will you be my valentine?"
St. Patrick's Day is in March.
"Happy St. Patrick's Day!"
April Fool's Day is in April.
"Ha-ha-ha, April fool!"
Mother's Day is in May.
"Mommy, we love you."
Father's Day is in June.
"Daddy, we love you."
The American Independence Day is in July.
"Wow! Fireworks!"
My birthday is in August.
"Happy birthday!"
School begins in September.
"Good morning, Mrs. Wood."
Halloween is in October.
"Trick or treat."
Thanksgiving is in November.
"Please pass the turkey."
Christmas is in December.
"Merry Christmas, everyone!"
Alice saw Grandma grabbing her coat.
"Where are you going?" she asked.
"I'm going to the homeless shelter," said Grandma.
"Want to come?"
"What will we do there?" asked Alice.
"Help some people," said Grandma.
"Okay," said Alice.
Grandma and Alice arrived at the shelter.
First, they painted the kitchen with other volunteers.
By lunchtime the walls were bright yellow.
"Beautiful!" said Alice. "What’s next?"
"Babysitting," said Grandma.
"Several moms live here.
One has to go to work.
We’re going to take care of her son."
Alice read Nick a dinosaur book.
The little boy followed Alice everywhere.
"My birthday is tomorrow," said Nick.
"Will you have a party?" asked Alice.
"No," said Nick quietly.
Alice thought about her birthday.
"I always have a party," Alice thought.
Suddenly Alice knew what to do.
The next day Alice and Grandma found Nick.
Alice gave him a big box.
Nick opened it and saw a dinosaur toy!
There were also candles, balloons, and a cake.
"It's a birthday box!" cried Nick.
"When does my party start?"
Alice grinned. "Right now!"
Autumn is my favorite season.
There are so many things to do.
I can't wait!
The leaves change color in autumn.
Yellow, brown, red, and orange!
I like to watch the leaves fall down.
Then I like to jump in them!
My family goes apple picking.
This red apple tastes sweet.
This green one tastes sour.
Autumn apples are so delicious!
Look! There's a corn maze.
I go inside.
I go left. I go right.
Oh no! I'm lost.
Dad helps me find my way.
Next we go to a pumpkin patch.
I pick the largest pumpkin.
Later my sister draws a scary face on it.
Dad carves the pumpkin.
Mom lights a candle inside.
Now we have a jack-o'-lantern!
We dress in costumes for Halloween.
I'm a scary monster.
My friend is a silly clown.
We walk around the neighborhood.
"Trick or treat!" we say to our neighbors.
Then they give us candy!
The weather is getting colder.
Now autumn is over.
Good-bye, autumn.
See you next year!
I’m lonely. I’m bored. And I’m really sad.
I’m stuck in my room . And I’m getting mad.
My friends are playing. And I’m in my bed.
I can’t play outside with this broken leg!
If I had wings, I would fly high in the sky.
I would fly to the birds. I’d even say, "Hi!"
If I had fins, I would swim deep in the sea.
I would look for treasure. It would be all for me.
If I had a horse, I would ride through the mountains.
I would stop for water. I’d drink from the fountains.
If I had a sailboat, I would sail on the water.
I would see dolphins and whales. I’d even see otters.
If I had an airplane, I would fly to faraway lands.
I would stop in the desert. I’d see a huge cactus in the sand.
But I don’t have wings. I have none of these things.
I have one broken leg. It’s stuck in a sling.
Wait! There’s a knock at my door.
One friend, two friends, three friends, four!
Summer vacation starts tomorrow.
My family has so many plans!
We'll visit an amusement park.
I'm going to ride a roller coaster. Whee!
We'll visit a forest.
I'm going to catch fish in the lake.
We'll visit an island.
I'm going to swim in the ocean.
We'll visit a big city.
I'm going to see a science museum.
We'll visit an aquarium.
I'm going to meet dolphins.
We'll visit a water park.
I'm going to ride a waterslide.
I'm so excited!
What will you do this summer?
At school we speak English.
But we speak many other languages too.
Mrs. Berman is from Germany.
"Good morning, class," she says.
"Good morning," we say in German. "Guten Morgen!"
Koji's grandfather is from Japan.
He visits our classroom.
We say "welcome" in Japanese. "Yōkoso."
Mr. Como is from Italy.
He is our music teacher.
We sing "hello" in Italian. "Ciao!"
David is from China.
He brings dumplings from home.
We say "thank you" in Chinese. "Xie-xie."
Jane's friend lives in France.
Jane teaches us words in French.
Au revoir means "good-bye."
Miss Isabel is from Spain.
She makes hot soup for lunch.
"Yum!" we say in Spanish. "Es rico!"
Hana is from Korea.
She shows us how to write in Korean.
I write "mom." "Umma."
I can speak many languages.
What languages can you speak?
Day 1, August 5
We moved into our cabins today.
"I want the top bunk!"
Day 2, August 6
We went on a hike at half past eight.
"Ouch! Mosquito bites!"
We played volleyball at a quarter past two.
"The blue team wins!"
Day 3, August 7
We rowed canoes at half past ten.
"Let's race!"
We made clay mugs at two.
"Wow! Yours looks great!"
Day 4, August 8
We had a bonfire at a quarter to seven.
"Who wants s'mores?"
Bob told scary stories at half past eight.
"The monster was very hairy . . ."
Day 5, August 9
Today was the last day of camp.
"See you next year, Bob and Liz!"

19.title: In the Middle of the Night

paragraphs.text: In the middle of the night, some people are busy.
The nurses take care of patients.
The police officers patrol the streets.
The truck drivers deliver boxes.
The pilots fly airplanes.
The printers print newspapers.
The bakers bake bread and cakes.
In the middle of the night, some people are busy.
But it is quiet everywhere.

20.title: No Two People Are the Same

paragraphs.text: No two people are the same.
We have different skin colors.
I have light skin.
He has dark skin.
We have different eye colors.
I have green eyes.
He has brown eyes.
She has blue eyes.
We have different hair colors.
I have blond hair.
He has black hair.
She has brown hair.
We have different body shapes.
He is tall.
She is short.
We have different abilities too.
I can run fast.
He can kick well.
She can sing beautifully.
We are all very different.
No two people are the same.
All people are special!
Where is the ball?
Is it behind the curtain?
No, it isn't.
There's a backpack behind the curtain.
Is it under the dresser?
No, it isn't.
There's a wallet under the dresser.
Is it in front of the cabinet?
No, it isn't.
There's a pen in front of the cabinet.
Is it on the couch?
No, it isn't.
There's an alarm clock on the couch.
Is it beside the fireplace?
No, it isn't.
There's a broom beside the fireplace.
Is it between the flowerpots?
No, it isn't.
There's a glove between the flowerpots.
Is it in the dog house?
Yes, it is.
The ball is in the dog house.
I found the ball!
My friends and I are good at sports.
We do many different kinds of them.
Ashley is good at skiing.
She speeds down the hill on her skis.
Josh is good at surfing.
He rides the waves with his surfboard.
Nicole is good at horseback riding.
She jumps fences with her horse.
Cody is good at table tennis.
He hits the tiny ball with his paddle.
Yuna is good at skating.
She jumps and spins on her skates.
I'm good at taekwondo.
I can kick high and punch fast.
What sports are you good at?
I like to go camping.
Camping is not like staying at home.
At the campground, I stay in a tent.
At home, I stay in my room.
At the campground, my dad watches birds.
At home, he reads books about birds.
At the campground, my mom cooks over a campfire.
At home, she cooks on the stove.
At the campground, I watch stars from the hill.
At home, I watch stars from the porch.
At the campground, I sleep in a sleeping bag.
At home, I sleep in my bed.
At the campground, I get water from the stream.
At home, I get water from the faucet.
At the campground, I hike in the woods.
At home, I walk on the sidewalk.
I have fun because camping is different!
It was Yoo Jin's first day at school.
Yoo Jin's mom kissed her cheek and patted her head.
"Don't be scared, sweetheart," Mom said.
"School is fun."
Yoo Jin held her new bag.
She had new pencils, books, and erasers.
Yoo Jin was happy and scared.
Yoo Jin saw the big girls.
They were on the swings.
They were on the seesaw.
The girls skipped.
They sang, "Dance, laugh, and learn too. Come and play! Don't be blue!"
Yoo Jin ran to the girls.
She sat on the seesaw.
She got on the swing.
Yoo Jin skipped.
Yoo Jin sang, "Dance, laugh, and learn too. Come and play. Don't be blue!"
It was Yoo Jin's first day of school.
She loved it!
If I had a hot air balloon,
I could fly around the world.
I could fly to China.
I could see the Great Wall and pandas.
I could fly to Australia.
I could see koalas and kangaroos.
I could fly to France.
I could see the Eiffel Tower and eat baguettes.
I could fly to Holland.
I could see windmills and tulips.
I could fly to Egypt.
I could see pyramids and the Nile River.
I could fly to England.
I could see the Tower of London and Big Ben.
I could fly to America.
I could see the Statue of Liberty and New York City.
I could fly to Switzerland.
I could see the Alps and skiers.
If you had a hot air balloon, where could you fly?
In the summer I build sand castles.
In the winter I build snowmen.
In the summer I have water fights with my friends.
In the winter I have snowball fights with my friends.
In the summer I drink cold juice.
In the winter I drink hot chocolate.
In the summer I roll down the hills.
In the winter I sled down the hills.
In the summer I go on picnics with my family.
In the winter I go skiing with my family.
In the summer I swim in the lake.
In the winter I skate on the frozen lake.
In the summer I turn on the fan.
In the winter I turn on the heater.
What do you like to do in the summer?
What do you like to do in the winter?
In the city we hear pigeons cooing.
In the country we hear cows mooing.
In the city we hear airplanes roaring.
In the country we hear crickets chirping.
In the city we hear car horns honking.
In the country we hear chickens clucking.
In the city we hear traffic zooming.
In the country we hear tractors chugging.
In the city we hear children laughing.
In the country we hear children laughing too.
In the city we hear grandparents telling stories.
In the country we hear grandparents telling stories too.
In the city we hear parents saying "I love you."
In the country we hear parents saying "I love you" too.
Where do you live?
What sounds do you hear?
If I were a pilot,
I could fly a plane.
If I were a doctor,
I could help sick people get better.
If I were a fisherman,
I could catch many fish.
If I were a police officer,
I could catch criminals.
If I were a builder,
I could build houses.
If I were a farmer,
I could grow rice.
If I were a teacher,
I could teach children how to read.
What do you want to be?
Long ago life was different.
Long ago people rode horses to work.
Now we ride in cars.
Long ago people sent someone to deliver letters.
Now we send emails on our computers.
Long ago people used lanterns and candles.
Now we use electric lights.
Long ago people got water with buckets.
Now we get water from faucets.
Long ago people cooked on fires.
Now we cook on stoves.
Long ago people cleaned with brooms.
Now we clean with vacuum cleaners.
Long ago people washed clothes by hand.
Now we wash clothes with washing machines.
Long ago people drew pictures by hand.
Now we use cameras to take pictures.
Long ago life was different.
We have many toys.
We all have favorite toys.
My big brother's favorite toy is his drums.
He plays the drums and sings songs to us.
My little brother's favorite toy is his truck.
He pushes the truck around the house.
My sister's favorite toy is her baby doll.
She holds her baby doll.
My friend Johnny's favorite toy is his doctor kit.
He comes to our house and takes care of us.
My friend Lisa's favorite toy is her tea set.
She serves us tea with her tea set.
My friend Mike's favorite toy is his ball.
He likes to throw it and catch it.
My favorite toy is my camera.
I take pictures of everyone with their toys.
I am a baker.
I bake bread, cake, and cookies.
Today I am baking chocolate chip cookies.
You can help me!
First we need a large bowl.
We put butter in the bowl.
We add sugar, eggs, and vanilla.
Let's stir, stir, stir!
Now we pour in flour.
Next come salt and baking soda.
Then we stir again.
We add the chocolate chips.
We stir a few more times, and . . .
Look! We made cookie dough!We scoop up dough.
We drop spoonfuls of dough on a tray.
The cookies bake in the oven.
Are they ready yet?
No, not yet!
Brring!
In ten minutes our cookies are ready.
Mmm . . .
I think chocolate chip cookies are yummy!
Do you like them too?
What you need to make yummy cookies:
225 grams of butter
1 cup brown sugar
1/2 cup white sugar
2 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla
2 1/4 cups flour
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon baking soda
350 grams chocolate chips
Spring, summer, fall, and winter are the four seasons.
The seasons are different and they have special friends.
Spring said, "I'm warm. Plants love me because I give them rain."
Drip drop, drip drop.
Spring said, "The butterflies love me because I give them flowers."
Red flowers, yellow flowers.
Summer said, "I'm very hot. The sea loves me because people swim in the sea."
Splish splash, splish splash.
Summer said, "Ice cream loves me because people eat ice cream."
Strawberry flavor, vanilla flavor.
Fall said, "I'm cool. The leaves love me because I give them pretty colors."
Red, orange, and yellow.
Fall said, "The squirrels love me because I give them nuts."
Pick up, pick up.
Winter said, "I'm very cold. The snow loves me because children play in the snow."
Snowflakes, snowflakes.
Winter said, "The sleds love me because children go sledding."
Weee! Weee!
Spring, summer, fall, and winter are happy seasons.
They are happy because they have special friends.
Today my family is going to Chinatown.
It's the Chinese New Year.
So we will see a parade!
First my brother and I spot some sweets.
Mom buys a few for us.
"Mmm!" I say. "Delicious!"
Next we hear some drummers.
We clap when the drummers play Chinese music.
Whoa! Here comes a dancing dragon!
Dad says dragons are special in China.
They bring good luck in the new year.
Then acrobats spin plates round and round.
I worry that one will fall!
But the acrobats are amazing.
They don't drop any plates at all!
Later Chinese lanterns glow in the night.
Mom says they are beautiful.
They're my favorite thing until I see something else.
Fireworks!
Boom ! Boom !
Bright colors sparkle in the sky.
When it's time to go, I feel sad.
But dad says we can come back next year.
"Hooray!" I cheer. "Happy New Year!"
Today is a special day for our family.
It is Grandma's birthday.
We are going to have a birthday party!
Don't tell Grandma! The party is a surprise!
Everybody has a job to do.
My sister keeps Grandma busy outside.
Mom bakes a birthday cake.
Dad decorates the room.
I set the table.
My younger brother peeks out the window.
He watches for Grandma.
"Are we ready now? We have the cake, the birthday card, the gifts, and the candles."
"Yes, we are ready."
"Now whistle to your sister."
Then she brings Grandma inside.
Now here comes Grandma! "Surprise!"
"Oh my!"
"Grandma, blow out the candles!"
"Make a wish too!"
"Okay, my dears!"
We all sing "Happy Birthday" to Grandma.
Grandma has a big, big smile!
I have some ice cream.
But I don't have any chocolate syrup.
I have some cookies.
But I don't have any milk.
I have some strawberries.
But I don't have any whipped cream!
I put some ice cream in my bowl.
I put some cookies in my bowl.
I put some strawberries in my bowl.
A delicious sundae!
Tala's parents are from the Philippines.
They are Filipino.
When I go to her house, we eat shaved ice.
It is sweet and delicious.
Carolina's parents are from Germany.
They are German.
When I play at her house, we eat sausage!
It is salty and delicious.
Uri's parents are from Israel.
They are Israeli.
When he comes over, he brings sesame snacks.
They are crunchy and delicious!
Elsa's parents are from Sweden.
They are Swedish.
When I go to her house, we eat rice pudding.
It is creamy and delicious.
Tala, Carolina, Uri, Elsa, and I are in the same class.
We are all friends.
Tomorrow is my sixth birthday.
I want a big birthday party.
I want a birthday party at the roller rink.
"Whee!"
I want a birthday party with lots of balloons.
"Pop! Pop! Pop!"
I want a birthday party with lots of presents.
"Wow, thanks!"
I want a birthday party with lots of games.
"I win!"
I want a birthday party with lots of pizza.
"I love pizza!"
I want a birthday party with lots of ice cream.
"Yummy!"
I can't wait until tomorrow!
It will be lots of fun!
I like to climb. Do you like climbing too?
In the park, I like to climb up high in the trees.
At the beach, I like to climb on the big rocks.
At the playground, I like to climb on the jungle gym.

"Wow! Your birthday cake is beautiful," said Bob.
"It has so many layers! Who made it?"
"Well," I said. "A farmer grew the wheat.
A miller changed the wheat into flour.
A chicken laid the eggs.
And a cow gave the milk.
So they helped make my cake.
"A truck driver delivered the flour, eggs, and milk.
A clerk sold them to my mother.
My mother brought them home.
So they helped too.
"My grandmother put everything into a bowl.
She mixed the flour, eggs, and milk.
Then she poured it into a baking pan.
My sister put the pan into the oven.
After thirty minutes she took it out.
So they also helped.
"Then I put the icing on the cake.
So I helped too.
We all helped make it."
"Wow!" said Bob.
"Many people helped make your cake.
But it's not finished yet!"
"What do you mean?" I asked.
"It looks finished to me."
"It doesn't have candles!" said Bob.
"I'll put some on.
I helped too!
Happy Birthday!"

Ed looks at his uniform. He is very surprised.
The coat is too long. The pants are too short.
The shoes are too big. The hat is too small.
"Mom! My uniform doesn't fit," Ed says.
Ed's mother looks at the clothes.
"Everything is perfect. Let me help you," she says and smiles.
"There you are, dear." She paints his face.
His mouth is bigger.
"Here is a tear under your eye. Here is a red nose.
Here is a funny hat," says his mother.
Ed looks in the mirror. He is very happy.
"Am I a clown?" he asks.
"No," says his mother. "You just look like a clown!"
Ed walks to clown school with two smiles.
One smile is painted. And one smile is real.
